entities.span: This project's default build approach is Tracer Bullet (a thin end to end slice proven before scaling). Applied here: prove the whole real path, real vendor call, real verdict, real report, on exactly one pair before scaling to all sixteen and the cross pair and aggregate logic.

Add the `eval` Vitest project to `vitest.config.mts`: `extends: true`, `include: ["test/eval/**/*.test.ts"]`, `environment: "node"`, the shared `setupFiles`, `globalSetup: ["./test/setup/require-stack.ts"]`, `testTimeout: 300_000`, `hookTimeout: 60_000`, `maxConcurrency: 4`, and `fileParallelism: false` scoped to this project alone. Add the `"eval": "vitest run --project eval"` script to `package.json`. Satisfies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-11**.
rejected_spans: (pulls in the root `resolve.tsconfigPaths` and the `server-only` alias every other project already relies on; omitting it is exactly the failure Option 2 was rejected for, since `scoreListing()`'s own `import "server-only"` throws without it)
(five sequential `ai_scoring` calls at its own 30 second `timeoutMs` ceiling each, plus headroom, since one pair's test body cannot finish faster than its slowest rerun)
(the fixture user mint against a possibly cold stack)
(a real, installed Vitest 4.1.11 option bounding how many pairs' test bodies run at once; set explicitly rather than left at whatever the installed version currently defaults to)

the same reason `integration-serial` already carries it: this project is written to hold exactly one file sharing one minted session and one report writer, and a second file here would run in a separate worker by Vitest's own default, mint a second session, and race the first on the same report filename

entities.span: Export `resolvedModel()` from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts`, and add `bandAnchorsHash()` as a small pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts`. Write the pure verdict logic in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`: the three way outcome classification (refusal, rerun failure, scored success) from AC-3, the majority vote with the 3 of 5 inconclusive floor and the no majority/`acceptableBands` exception, the distinct `stability-probe` "every success inside `acceptableBands`" rule (AC-4), and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison (AC-5). Wire `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts` against constructed fixtures for each rule, no vendor call involved. Satisfies **AC-3**, **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-6**.
rejected_spans: (lifted from the equivalent already written, but currently private to `src/lib/ai/tiers.test.ts`, which switches to importing it instead of keeping its own copy)

entities.span: The thin thread: `test/eval/harness.test.ts`, one `describe("eval harness")`, a top level `beforeAll` running `validateGroundTruth()` (throwing with every issue if any, before anything else) then minting the one fixture session for the run; one `it.concurrent` per pair named `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` ``, whose body awaits five sequential `scoreListing()` calls, feeds the outcomes to step 2's verdict function, stores the result in a module scoped `Map<string, PairVerdict>` keyed by pair id, and asserts that the verdict's status is `pass`, so `fail` and `inconclusive` both fail their own test with the denominator and distribution in the message; and a final `afterAll` that runs the preference leak check against the map, writes the JSON report (including the model id and anchors hash), then deletes the fixture user. Prove this against exactly `control-direct-match` (real vendor calls) before scaling: get `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` green end to end. Satisfies the first slice of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-9**.
rejected_spans: (via the test context's own `expect`, required under `it.concurrent`)

entities.span: Scale to the full sixteen pairs, confirm `maxConcurrency` and `fileParallelism` behave as designed under a real, unfiltered `pnpm eval` run, and confirm the run's own exit code is non zero on a fail, an inconclusive pair, a leak, or an abort, and zero only when everything that ran passed cleanly. Satisfies the rest of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-7**, **AC-8**.

Add the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test under `src/features/scoring/eval/` (the ordinary unit project, no vendor call): a literal `toEqual` pin of today's text plus a `bandAnchorsHash()` equality check, both failing by name, pointing at spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes. Satisfies **AC-10**.
